visual_correlations.comment: The speaker began the video with an introduction of full bridge rectifiers before stating that, despite successfully being able to convert AC power to DC with the aid of an electrolytic capacitor, there is a noticeable voltage drop in this conversion. The voltage drops occurs when heat dissipates from the full-bridge rectifier and/or electrolytic capacitor. The speaker in the video works to mitigate the problem of voltage drop by utilizing an active rectifier which replaces the diodes with MOSFET switches despite MOSFETs not behaving exactly like diodes. To work around this, existing chips were used so that the circuit would only turn on diagonal MOSFET switches simultaneously in order to more closely behave like a full-bridge rectifier. The active rectifier proved to be more efficient but not significantly so.
